angles.title: The starter is the whole bakery
angles.thesis: The slow, invisible part of the work, the part that happens before anyone sees anything, decides the result.

uses.quote: the first month they are not allowed to shape a single loaf
You can't rescue bad fermentation with good scoring.
the failure happened twelve hours before they touched the dough
the patience of reading back through your own records instead of guessing
Not his shaping, not his scoring, the fact that he noticed the starter.
the bread part is really about patience with the slow invisible part of the work, the part that happens before anyone sees anything

angles.title: The agenda is upside down
angles.thesis: Status updates belong in a short written document; the weekly meeting should exist only for decisions and disagreements, and be cancelled when there are none.
angles.audience: the writer's own team and its managers

uses.quote: half the agenda is status updates that could be a written document
we spent seventy minutes on updates and twenty minutes on the one decision that actually mattered
The thing that needs the whole room gets the least time.
the Monday meeting is only for decisions and disagreements. If there is no decision on the agenda, we cancel the meeting.
each update is three lines, what changed, what is blocked, what decision you need
the meeting facilitator should change every week

open_questions: Is this a proposal to the team, or an essay for outsiders about meetings in general?
How should the managers' objection (the meeting is where they feel informed) be answered?

angles.title: Write the toolbox, not the thesis
angles.thesis: Essays reach readers through one small, concrete object or person; the big idea has to arrive on its own, or not at all.
angles.audience: people who write in public, and the writer's own newsletter readers

uses.quote: I have a feeling, not an argument.
The essays that actually landed with readers were all small and concrete.
I think I start big because I want the essay to matter, and small feels like it does not matter.
nobody would have read an essay titled inheritance and silence
start with one object or one person, and let the big idea show up on its own by the end, or not at all. Write the toolbox, not the thesis.

angles.title: The small invisible daily thing

uses.quote: The small invisible daily thing, the starter, the notebook, the toolbox. Maybe that is the actual essay. I don't know yet. Is it one piece or three pieces? I genuinely can't tell.
the slow invisible part of the work
So why do I keep starting with the abstract?

open_questions: What does the combined piece argue? The memo names a shared image (the starter, the notebook, the toolbox) but not a claim that joins them.
Does the meeting material belong in it? The memo never connects the meeting to the bakery or the essays.
Is the toolbox essay already published material to reuse, or only to mention?
